why: All three checks confirm the finding; nothing refutes it. (1) QUOTE IS VERBATIM. curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp.md returns the sentence character-for-character on line 108 (Python substring test: True). Note: a first curl produced a truncated 33 KB body; the full 80 866-byte fetch is the one verified. Reading the WHOLE line does not reverse the conclusion, it strengthens it — the line is five sentences: 'CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is the stable project root and doesn't change when you add or remove working directories mid-session. A server that limits its own filesystem access to a set of allowed directories should implement the MCP roots/list request instead. Claude Code answers roots/list with the session's launch directory plus every [additional working directory](/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) you've granted with --add-dir, /add-dir, or the additionalDirectories setting. Claude Code sends notifications/roots/list_changed when that set changes. Before v2.1.203, roots/list returned only the launch directory and Claude Code didn't send notifications/roots/list_changed.' The second sentence explicitly routes allowed-directory scoping to roots/list rather than to the project-dir env var, and the fourth sentence independently confirms the list_changed half of the claimed behaviour. (2) CITED CODE MATCHES. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:310-324 constructs `new Client({name:'nessy-agent',version:'1.0.0'}, {capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? {elicitation:{form:{},url:{}}} : {}})`. The only capability ever declared is elicitation, and only when a handler is supplied; the R24 comment above it states the policy 'advertise only what we honour'. packages/shared/src/mcp/__tests__/client-transport.test.ts:78-90 pins that surface exactly (`sdkClient._capabilities.elicitation` toEqual `{form:{},url:{}}`, undefined without a handler) — so the capability set is deliberately narrow and roots is not in it. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, and it holds. Absence: `grep -ra` (NUL-safe) for roots/list, ListRoots, listRoots, sendRootsListChanged, RootsListChangedNotification over packages/ and apps/ returns ZERO hits in Nessy source. The only hits are inside built bundles and third-party binaries, and each was opened and confirmed to be the vendored MCP SDK's own protocol table, not an implementation: packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js and apps/electron/dist/resources/bridge-mcp-server/index.js each contain `ListRootsRequestSchema = RequestSchema.extend({method: literal("roots/list")})` plus its entry in `ServerRequestSchema`, with `setRequestHandler(ListRoots` count = 0 in both; the remaining hits are the prebuilt codex-app-server binaries. No `registerCapabilities` call exists anywhere in the repo, so nothing adds roots after construction either. LAYER UP — is something upstream already handling it? No, and this is the check that could have refuted it. Nessy's pool is the ONLY MCP client that connects third-party servers, so no host SDK's roots implementation is ever in the path: claude-agent.ts:1136-1150 builds `Options['mcpServers']` from in-process `sourceProxies` ('Per-source proxy servers from centralized MCP pool… the pool owns all source connections centrally', claude-agent.ts:474-477) rather than handing raw MCP configs to the Claude SDK, and mcp/pool-server.ts:211-213 re-exposes the same pool to Codex/Pi as `nessy-pool-proxy` with `capabilities: {tools:{listChanged:true}}`. LAYER DOWN — sibling MCP clients omit roots too, so there is no other client that answers: api-source-pool-client.ts:20 passes no capabilities argument at all and validation.ts:411-413 passes `capabilities: {}`. SIBLING-SUBSYSTEM TRAP checked and cleared: the ~60 other `roots` hits in the repo are unrelated same-name symbols in different subsystems — sandbox/filesystem containment (session-tools-core credential-deny-roots.ts, pi-harness/isolation.ts), `--add-dir` memory-file scoping (capabilities/native-sources.ts), test temp-dir arrays, Codex FuzzyFileSearchParams.roots, and client.ts:886's own 'plugin-mcp-working-directory-outside-authorized-roots' (which contains where a plugin MCP PROCESS is launched, and never reaches the wire as a roots/list answer). NOT AN OWNER DECISION: the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 are SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, and listSessionSummaries — none is MCP roots. The parity audit corroborates rather than excuses: 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1787 lists roots/list among grep-absence claims 're-confirmed absent repo-wide at the time', and grep over docs/ finds no plan and no parity row for it. NOT A DELIBERATE FORK DIFFERENCE: this touches no dropped subscription flow, no gateway routing and no rename — and the fork already owns the exact inputs a roots/list answer needs, so this is a missing surface rather than a missing concept: `additionalDirectories` is a first-class persisted setting (config/storage.ts:132, config/validators.ts:191/227) resolved by packages/shared/src/agent/additional-directories.ts into a `roots: string[]`, and `--add-dir` roots are already modelled in capabilities/types.ts:197-201. One imprecision in the original wording, too small to refute: it is the SERVER that sends `roots/list` to the client, not the client that requests it; the accurate mechanism is that without the declared capability a spec-compliant server never asks, and a server that asked anyway would get a 'Method not found' because no ListRootsRequestSchema handler is registered.
correctedState: Nessy never exposes MCP roots to any server. packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:310-324 declares `capabilities: options?.elicitationHandler ? { elicitation: { form: {}, url: {} } } : {}` — `roots` is never declared, no `ListRootsRequestSchema` handler is registered, `sendRootsListChanged` is never called, and no `registerCapabilities` call adds it later; client-transport.test.ts:78-90 pins the elicitation-only capability set. The two sibling MCP clients omit it as well (api-source-pool-client.ts:20 passes no capabilities argument; validation.ts:411-413 passes `capabilities: {}`). Repo-wide `grep -ra` finds `roots/list`/`ListRoots` only in the vendored MCP SDK protocol tables inside built bundles (packages/pi-agent-server/dist/index.js, apps/electron/dist/resources/bridge-mcp-server/index.js — `setRequestHandler(ListRoots` count 0 in both) and in the prebuilt codex-app-server binaries, never in Nessy source. The consequence holds for every backend because Nessy's own pool is the sole MCP client that connects third-party servers — claude-agent.ts:1136-1150 hands the Claude SDK in-process pool proxies instead of raw MCP configs, and mcp/pool-server.ts:211-213 re-exposes the same pool to Pi/Codex — so no host SDK's roots implementation is ever in the path. Precise mechanism: because the client advertises no `roots` capability, a spec-compliant server never sends `roots/list`, and one that sent it anyway would receive 'Method not found'; `notifications/roots/list_changed` is likewise never emitted. A server that scopes its own filesystem access via roots therefore gets nothing. The inputs already exist — `additionalDirectories` is persisted (config/storage.ts:132, validators.ts:191/227) and resolved into a `roots: string[]` by agent/additional-directories.ts, and `--add-dir` roots are modelled in capabilities/types.ts:197-201 — so this is an unimplemented surface, not a deliberate deviation: it is absent from inert-worklist §3's nine owner decisions and has no parity row or plan, while 2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1787 independently re-confirms it absent.
